entries.title: Unavailable embeds show a plain, translated message instead of "[object Object]"
entries.summary: When a schedule, speaker list, or other embed widget cannot load — for example because the embed ID was deleted or is unknown — visitors now see a plain sentence in the page's language: **"This schedule isn't available right now."**, **"This speaker list isn't available right now."**, or **"This content isn't available right now."** The raw API error text and the broken `[object Object]` string no longer appear. The message is translated into German, French and Spanish. Integrators still receive the technical reason via the `sb-embed-error` event and the browser console.

where.path: Sessions → Embeds → embed widget on your website

entries.use_case: Any attendee who lands on an event website while an embed is misconfigured or has been deleted now sees a polite, localised message rather than a confusing technical error string — protecting the organiser's brand without requiring any action on their part.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their embedded agenda or speaker list is showing a broken error message to website visitors.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Embeds V2 on their event website.
internal.gotchas: The fix is automatic — no embed attributes, CSS properties or script URLs changed. The content-gallery widget is unaffected and keeps its own error messages.
internal.talk_track: If an embed ever fails to load, your website visitors now see a friendly sentence in their language instead of a raw technical error.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note what visitors see when an embed cannot load, and that integrators can catch the technical reason with the sb-embed-error event and the browser console.

entries.title: Site sign-in links show "Continue as <email>" before opening the portal
entries.summary: When a reviewer, submitter or speaker opens a magic sign-in link for any Site (including Platform Sites), they now see a **Continue as <email>** confirmation screen before being taken into the portal. If the link has expired, the screen offers **Send a new link** instead of an error.

where.path: Any Site sign-in link (reviewer portal, speaker portal, submission portal)

entries.use_case: Reviewers and speakers who share a device or browser with colleagues can confirm they are signing in as the right person before landing in the portal, reducing accidental cross-account access.

cs_action.note: Every customer's reviewers and submitters will see one extra screen when they open a Site sign-in link. No action needed to enable it, but CS should be ready to explain the new screen if customers ask.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that reviewers or speakers are confused by a new screen when opening their portal link, or asks why there is an extra step.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers using magic-link sign-in for reviewer, speaker or submission portals.
internal.gotchas: This is on by default for all Sites, including Platform Sites. There is no way to disable it per event.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers and speakers now see a quick confirmation screen when they open their sign-in link, so they always know which account they are entering — and if the link has expired, they can request a new one right there.

draft.docs_gap: Guide should document the new "Continue as <email>" confirmation screen and the "Send a new link" expired-link flow.
draft.why_use_it: Magic sign-in links let participants, reviewers and speakers reach their portal without a password. The confirmation screen makes it clear which account the link belongs to, so people on shared devices or with multiple email addresses always land in the right place. An expired link offers a one-click way to request a fresh one, removing a common support request.

entries.title: New layout options for agenda and speaker embeds on self-serve Sessions
entries.summary: Self-serve Sessions organizers can now embed their agenda and speaker gallery using three purpose-built layouts: **Simple** (a clean schedule and speaker wall), **Grid** (rooms as columns with time down the side, using room names from your event), and **List** (a speaker gallery list view). Add the `layout="simple"`, `layout="grid"`, or `layout="list"` attribute to your embed code to choose a layout. Existing Platform embeds without a `layout` attribute are unchanged.
entries.use_case: A self-serve Sessions customer who wants to display their agenda on their conference website can pick the Grid layout to show rooms as columns, or the Simple layout for a clean, minimal schedule — without needing custom CSS or developer work.

cs_action.note: These layouts are available only when the web-api payload carries self_serve.product === 'sessions', which is sent only for self-serve orgs. Platform orgs are unaffected. PROD has not been published yet — this PR deploys to DEV only; a manual workflow_dispatch is required for staging and PROD US/EU/ME.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a self-serve Sessions customer asks how to embed their agenda or speaker list on their website and wants a cleaner or more structured layout than the default.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Sessions customers who embed their program on an external website.
internal.staff_path: Program → Embeds — add layout="simple", layout="grid", or layout="list" to the embed snippet
internal.gotchas: Not yet published to PROD; DEV only at merge time. The layout attribute is opt-in — omitting it keeps the existing embed rendering unchanged. Grid layout pulls room names from locationsById on the event.
internal.talk_track: You can now choose how your agenda embed looks on your website — a simple schedule, a room-by-room grid, or a speaker list — just by adding one attribute to your embed code.

draft.docs_gap: The embeds guide should document the new layout attribute values (simple, grid, list), show example embed snippets for each, and note that grid uses room names from the event's room settings.
draft.why_use_it: Agenda and speaker embeds let you publish your live program directly on your own website, keeping it automatically in sync with Sessionboard. Choose the layout that fits your site's design: a simple schedule and speaker wall for a clean look, a room-grid view for multi-track conferences, or a list view for speaker galleries. Attendees always see up-to-date session and speaker information without any manual updates on your end.

entries.title: Open a public People's Choice vote in your awards program
entries.summary: A new **People's Choice** panel lets you open a public vote on any program. Set how many votes each visitor may cast per nomination, then share the link. Results appear alongside your reviewer scores. Organizers can also **Hide nominator and nominee names from reviewers** directly from the program settings.
entries.use_case: An association running an annual awards program wants to supplement its expert panel scores with audience enthusiasm — opening a public vote lets the community weigh in without giving them access to the full review process.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a self-serve Awards customer asks how to involve their broader community or audience in the selection process alongside their reviewer panel.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any self-serve Awards customer who wants a public-facing vote component in their program.
internal.gotchas: People's Choice is self-serve for Awards customers. The hide-nominator/nominee-names toggle is also new and lives in the program's review settings.
internal.talk_track: You can now open a public vote alongside your expert review — set a votes-per-nomination cap and share the link with your audience.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a dedicated section explaining how to open a People's Choice vote, configure votes-per-nomination, share the public link, and read the results alongside reviewer scores.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Awards lets you run the full awards lifecycle — nominations, blind review, scoring and winner announcement — in one place. People's Choice adds a public voting layer so your audience can participate alongside your expert reviewers, driving engagement and awareness for your program. You control how many votes each visitor can cast, keeping the results meaningful.

entries.title: Time a quiz and see scores from a human reviewer on your learning site
entries.summary: Quizzes on a learning site can now have a time limit. Learners see a start screen, a live countdown that accounts for any extra time granted to them, and a **Timed out** result if they run out of time. When a quiz uses written answers that a person scores, learners see a **Reviewing** notice while scoring is in progress, then the final result with an overall note and a note beside each answer.

enable.path: Course builder → Quiz → Quiz settings → Time limit

entries.use_case: Certification programs that need proctored or time-boxed assessments can set a time limit on any quiz; learners who need accommodations can be given extra time without changing the quiz for everyone else.

cs_action.note: Existing courses are unaffected unless the author sets a time limit or uses scored written answers. No action needed unless a customer asks.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer running certification or continuing-education courses asks about timed assessments or human-scored written answers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessionboard Learning for professional certification, CME, or any program that requires proctored or manually graded assessments.
internal.staff_path: Course builder → Quiz → Quiz settings → Time limit (for timed quizzes); score written answers via the Scoring queue in the Learning admin.
internal.gotchas: The countdown follows the server deadline, so it is not affected by the learner's local clock. Extra time per learner must be set before the attempt starts.
internal.talk_track: You can now put a time limit on any quiz and grant individual learners extra time for accommodations. If you use written-answer questions, learners see a 'Reviewing' notice and get the reviewer's notes right beside each answer when scoring is done.

draft.docs_gap: The guide at /sessionboard-learning/courses/timed-quizzes should document how to set a time limit, what learners see on the start screen and countdown, how timed-out attempts are displayed, and how to grant a learner extra time. The scored-answers flow (ReviewNotice and per-answer notes) should be covered in /sessionboard-learning/courses/score-written-answers.
draft.why_use_it: Timed quizzes let you run assessments that mirror real certification exams, where completing questions within a set window is part of the requirement. When answers need a human reviewer — such as written responses or file uploads — learners see exactly where their attempt stands and receive the reviewer's notes alongside their score once grading is complete. Together these tools give you the controls to run rigorous, accreditation-ready courses directly on your learning site.

entries.title: Read and manage the Learning question bank via the public API
entries.summary: Three new endpoints expose the Learning workspace **Question Bank** to org-wide API tokens: list questions (`GET …/question-bank`) with filtering by tags, keyword, and archived status; list tags (`GET …/question-bank/tags`); and create, update, archive, or restore questions (`POST …/question-bank/manage`). Event-scoped tokens receive `403 ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED`. Both `/v1/organization/:orgId/learning/workspace/…` and the token-resolved `/v1/learning/workspace/…` paths are supported.
entries.use_case: A learning administrator can sync their question bank with an external authoring tool or LMS — pulling all questions by tag, creating new ones in bulk, and archiving retired questions — without logging into Sessionboard.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Learning customer asks about integrating their existing question library or automating course content management via API.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning customers who maintain large question banks or use external authoring tools and want to sync content programmatically.
internal.gotchas: Only org-wide API tokens work; event-scoped tokens return 403 ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED. These routes are part of the Learning suite which must be enabled. Documentation is unreleased until the Learning suite ships.
internal.talk_track: You can now manage your entire question bank through the API — pull questions by tag, create or update questions in bulk, and archive old ones, all from your own systems.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section documenting the three public API endpoints (list questions, list tags, manage questions) including required scopes, supported query parameters, and the org-wide token requirement.
draft.why_use_it: The question bank lets you build a library of reusable quiz questions at the organization level and draw from it across any course. With API access you can manage that library programmatically — importing questions from an existing item bank, keeping questions in sync with an external authoring tool, or automating archival of outdated content at scale.

entries.title: Site builder opens in the role that sees the page, with an Invited guest preview option
entries.summary: The Site builder now opens in the role that best matches the page being edited. On a sign-in-only **Learning Site**, the builder opens as **Learner** so the hero and course blocks are immediately visible; switching to **Visitor** previews the sign-in form. On a **Marketing** event page, **View as** now includes **Invited guest** so editors can preview invite-only pages exactly as a guest arriving from an invitation sees them. On **Awards**, opening a page restricted to Reviewers or Nominees automatically previews as one of those roles. Picking a block that the current preview role cannot see either switches to the correct role with an explanatory note, or indicates the block is hidden on that page.
entries.use_case: An organizer building an invite-only Marketing event page can now preview it as an Invited guest without leaving the builder, catching layout or content issues that a Visitor would never see. A Learning site editor no longer has to manually switch roles just to see the hero block they are trying to edit.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that the Site builder always shows the sign-in form instead of their Learning site content, or that they cannot preview an invite-only Marketing page as a guest.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Marketing event page builder with invite-only pages, Learning site builders, and Awards site builders with role-restricted pages.
internal.staff_path: Site builder → View as (event or org site builder)
internal.gotchas: The Invited guest canvas behaviour (previewAs=invited treated as arriving from an invitation) requires the companion org-portal PR #315 to be merged; until then, Invited guest renders like Visitor in the canvas frame.
internal.talk_track: The builder now opens in the role that actually sees the page you are editing, and you can switch roles with one click to check every audience's experience before you publish.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the View as role selector, explain which default role each site type (Marketing, Learning, Awards) opens with, describe the Invited guest option for Marketing pages, and explain how picking a block from On this page can auto-switch the preview role.
draft.why_use_it: The Site builder lets you design and preview every page of your event, learning, or awards site from inside the admin. Switching **View as** roles shows you exactly what each audience — Visitor, Invited guest, Learner, Reviewer, or Nominee — sees when they arrive, so you can catch access gaps and layout issues before publishing. Picking any block in the **On this page** panel jumps the preview to the role that can see it, keeping your editing flow uninterrupted.

entries.title: Sign-up block, gated video, "Ask about this event", and Learning Site credits on public Sites
entries.summary: Four capabilities land on public Sites and the Learning Site. (1) A **Sign-up form** block lets visitors subscribe by email directly from a live Site page. (2) A **Video** block supports a gallery gate (shown before playback or at a time code), a play button, an end card, and tracked plays; a **Premiere** block adds a countdown, a room link, and a post-premiere **Register** card. (3) An **Ask about this event** box appears on event pages created after release, letting visitors ask questions and receive AI-generated answers. (4) The Learning Site now renders in German, Spanish and French; learners can claim credit with an attestation, view and print certificates, add a certificate to LinkedIn, search the catalog, and download a **My credits** transcript as PDF or Excel.

where.path: Sites → Site builder → Blocks (Sign-up, Video, Premiere); Sites → Event page (Ask about this event); Learning Site → Lesson / Certificate pages

entries.use_case: Organizers can capture email interest before registration opens with the Sign-up block, gate on-demand recordings behind a form, and let prospective attendees ask questions on the event page — all without leaving the Site. Learning Site learners can now claim credit, download transcripts, and share certificates on LinkedIn in their own language.

cs_action.note: Ask about this event is off for all existing event pages and on only for pages created after release. The sign-up and premiere blocks appear only where an admin adds them. Learning Site changes are live for all existing Learning Sites immediately.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about capturing leads from their public event page, gating recordings, or offering CE credit with multilingual support on their Learning Site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Marketing Sites for lead generation, customers running on-demand video libraries, and Learning Site customers with non-English learners.
internal.staff_path: Sites → Site builder → add a Sign-up, Video, or Premiere block; event page Ask box is auto-enabled on new pages only (flip existing pages via web-api if needed).
internal.gotchas: Ask about this event renders only when site-info returns ask_enabled === true; existing event pages have this set to false. Sign-up and Premiere blocks require the new web-api endpoints to be deployed first — they degrade gracefully to empty without them.
internal.talk_track: You can now collect email sign-ups, gate recordings behind a form, and let visitors ask questions right on your event page. Learning Site learners in Germany, Spain and France get a fully translated experience and can download their credit transcript or add a certificate to LinkedIn.

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should document the Sign-up block, Video gate/Premiere block, and Ask about this event box as distinct block types, including how ask_enabled is set on new vs. existing event pages. The Learning Site guide should cover the attestation credit-claim flow, PDF/Excel transcript download, and LinkedIn certificate sharing.
draft.why_use_it: The Site builder lets you publish a branded public presence for your event — registration pages, on-demand video, speaker and session listings — without writing code. Sign-up blocks, gated video, and the Ask box turn a static page into a lead-capture and engagement surface. The Learning Site gives learners a localised experience where they can track progress, claim continuing education credit, and share proof of completion.

entries.title: Generate Agenda refines an existing draft instead of starting over
entries.summary: When a draft already has placed sessions, **Generate Agenda** now runs in improve mode: it keeps valid placements, repairs broken ones, and moves sessions one at a time to a better slot — up to three passes. Only **pinned** sessions stay fixed. A draft with no placements, or an explicit **Generate from scratch** run, uses the original greedy solver unchanged.
entries.use_case: An organizer who has already generated a draft and manually adjusted a few sessions can re-run Generate Agenda to tighten the remaining schedule without losing their manual work. The solver moves only sessions that can genuinely improve, so hand-placed and pinned sessions stay where they are.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer complains that re-running Generate Agenda wipes out manual session placements or that they have to re-pin everything after each run.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using the Scheduler agent to build or iterate on a draft agenda.
internal.gotchas: Improve mode runs automatically when the draft already has placed, unpinned rows — there is no UI toggle. If the solver cannot find a strictly better placement for any session (e.g. a fully packed agenda where only swaps would help), it reports 'No improvements found' and leaves the draft unchanged. The guard also reverts pass results if the total objective score would decrease.
internal.talk_track: Re-running Generate Agenda now improves your existing draft rather than rebuilding from scratch, so your manual placements and pins are preserved and the solver only moves sessions it can genuinely improve.

draft.docs_gap: The Scheduler agent guide should document the three run modes (first, improve, from scratch), explain that improve mode activates automatically when placed sessions exist, describe the pin behaviour, and note the "No improvements found" outcome.
draft.why_use_it: The Scheduler agent builds a draft agenda automatically, placing sessions into rooms and time slots while respecting capacity, speaker availability, and the criteria you set. Use it to turn a blank grid into a working schedule in seconds, then iterate — each subsequent run refines what is already there rather than discarding your edits. Pin any session to lock it in place and let the agent optimise everything around it.

entries.title: Transcript preview lock and "Transcripts and slide video" upgrade module in Sessionboard Marketing
entries.summary: In the standalone Sessionboard Marketing product, the recording drawer now shows only the first 5 minutes of a transcript for self-serve plans, with a **"First 5 minutes"** note and an **Enterprise** chip reading "The full transcript is part of the Sessionboard platform." The chip links to the new **Transcripts and slide video** upgrade page, which shows simulated screens of full transcript, search, edit and speakers, download (TXT, DOCX, SRT, VTT) and publish, along with the workspace's own recording and hours-transcribed counts and a **Talk to us** button.

where.path: Marketing → Content → Library → (open a recording) → Transcript

entries.use_case: A marketing team on a self-serve Marketing plan sees the first 5 minutes of each session transcript and a clear path to upgrade to the Sessionboard platform for full transcripts, search, editing, speaker labelling and multi-format download.

cs_action.note: Self-serve Marketing customers who ask about full transcripts should be directed to the Transcripts and slide video upgrade page or to their CSM to discuss the platform. The transcript lock is server-gated (web-api #5202 must be deployed); until that ships, all customers see the full transcript as before.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A self-serve Marketing customer asks why their transcript is cut off or asks about full transcript access, speaker labels, download formats or slide video.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Sessionboard Marketing customers who are actively using recordings and want full transcript capabilities.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Content → Library → (open a recording) → Transcript — staff always see the full transcript; the lock only fires for self-serve plans once web-api #5202 is live.
internal.gotchas: The transcript lock requires the server-side trim from web-api #5202 to be deployed; without it the drawer renders as before and no lock is shown. The sidebar row for the Transcripts and slide video upgrade page is staff-only by default; a self-serve customer can reach the page only by following the Enterprise chip link from the drawer. Slide video is described in the upgrade module copy but no slide-video UI is built yet.
internal.talk_track: Your recordings already live in Marketing — upgrading to the Sessionboard platform unlocks the full transcript, speaker labels, keyword search, editing and download in every major caption format, plus slide video.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the transcript preview limit for self-serve plans, the Enterprise chip and its link to the upgrade page, and the full list of transcript capabilities (search, edit, speaker labels, download formats) available on the Sessionboard platform.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing turns your session recordings into searchable, editable transcripts so you can pull quotes, create clips and publish polished content without leaving the platform. The full transcript experience — including speaker labels, keyword search, editing and download in TXT, DOCX, SRT and VTT — is part of the Sessionboard platform. The upgrade module lets you see exactly what you get before you make the move.

entries.title: Full recording transcripts are now an Enterprise feature in Sessionboard Marketing
entries.summary: On a self-serve Sessionboard Marketing plan, the **Content** page, **Ask**, and the Public API now return only the first 5 minutes of a recording's transcript. A **transcript_preview** notice explains that the full transcript is part of the Sessionboard platform and shows how many lines are hidden. Organizers on a platform contract, or any org billed by contract, continue to see the complete transcript.
entries.use_case: A self-serve Marketing customer who wants to search, quote, or build AI-assisted content from a full session transcript will see a preview of the first 5 minutes and a prompt to upgrade to the Sessionboard platform. Platform customers and contract orgs are unaffected and continue to access the complete transcript.

cs_action.note: Self-serve Marketing orgs (those with an Org_Subscriptions row for 'marketing' and no active Org_Contracts row) will now see a truncated transcript and an upgrade prompt. No action needed for platform or contract customers — they are unaffected. Self-serve billing is DEV-only today, so no prod impact until self-serve orgs exist.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a self-serve Marketing customer asks why their transcript is cut off after 5 minutes, or when a prospect asks about full transcript access.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Sessionboard Marketing customers who want to use full transcripts for content creation — direct them to upgrade to the Sessionboard platform.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Content → Recordings → open a recording → transcript panel
internal.gotchas: Transcription still runs and is metered on every plan. Only what is shown to the caller is trimmed — clips, reels, quote cards and captions are still generated from the full transcript internally. The kill switch MARKETING_TRANSCRIPT_PREVIEW_DISABLED=true in Doppler disables the gate if needed. The platform Media service (transcript export, edits, words, chapters) is not gated by this change.
internal.talk_track: The full recording transcript — everything speakers said, searchable and ready for clips and quotes — is part of the Sessionboard platform. Self-serve Marketing gives you a 5-minute preview so you can see what's possible before upgrading.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document that self-serve Marketing plans show only the first 5 minutes of a transcript, explain the upgrade_preview notice that appears, and clarify that clips and other generated content are unaffected.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing transcribes your recordings and makes the text available across the Content page, Ask, and the API so you can search, quote, clip, and generate content from what was said. On the Sessionboard platform, the full transcript powers every downstream content tool — clips, quote cards, recaps, and AI-generated summaries — without any manual copy-paste. Upgrading to the platform unlocks the complete transcript for every recording in your library.
